## Verdict: APPROVE with notes (no finding or checklist FAIL at or above the important threshold; notes remain)

This PR is ready to merge. No reviewer and no checklist item found a defect at or above the important threshold, all 37 acceptance criteria were itemized, and what remains is suggestions plus ten checklist items that could not be settled by reading alone.
Rule applied: rule 6, below-threshold findings, checklist FAILs or INCONCLUSIVE items remain, so the verdict is APPROVE with notes

## Code Review Findings

### 🟡 Suggestion / Minor (10)

<details><summary>10 items</summary>

1. Two internal docs still say that caller metadata can supply only RLS predicate values: `docs/internal/database-connectors/row-level-security.md` line 190 and `docs/internal/authentication/overview.md` line 113. With a rule-set file configured, caller `_meta` also carries the rule-set, account and user keys that choose the guarding set. The diff does not touch either line. (raised by 1/6 agents)
2. In `docs/external/rule-sets.md`, the "Asking a Question Under a Rule Set" list is incomplete. It describes `Request refused: no such rule set` only as "the named set is not in the file", but the code also returns it for a name that is not a string or whole number. The list does not say that a `_meta` with more than 64 keys is refused as rule-set key missing. It also omits the conversation-owner and catalog-unconfirmed refusals. (raised by 1/6 agents)
3. In `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py`, the `frozen=True` record models (lines 77 to 214) still hold mutable `list` fields: `Binding.account_ids`, `TableRule.columns` and `predicate_columns`, `RuleSet.tables`, `RuleSetFile.rule_sets` and `Source.global_switches`. A caller could append to them after validation and bypass the load-time checks. No current caller does. (raised by 1/6 agents)
4. In `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py`, `LoadedRuleSets` (lines 242 to 265) is a mutable dataclass with public fields, and `CatalogConfirmation.confirmed` is a public `bool`. Setting it from outside would skip the catalog check, so the rule that only a passing check sets it is kept by convention only. (raised by 1/6 agents)
5. In `src/sqllens/rule_sets.py`, `RuleSetSelection` (lines 348 to 358) checks nothing when it is built, so it can hold states that `select_rule_set` would refuse. `RuleSetGuardRunner._rewrite` trusts any published selection and does not check confirmation. The only producer today is `select_rule_set`. (raised by 1/6 agents)
6. In `src/sqllens/config.py`, `RuleSetsConfig._loaded` (lines 770 to 782) is set from outside the class by `Config._load_rule_sets`, so `file` and `loaded` can drift apart if `file` is changed after load. (raised by 1/6 agents)
7. In `tests/unit/test_query_database_rule_sets.py`, no test checks that `list_data_sources` answers a call with no `_meta` while a rule-set file is configured (criterion 32). (raised by 1/6 agents)
8. In `tests/unit/test_query_database_rule_sets.py`, the `show_details` profile case (criterion 34) is only checked for the selection, not end to end through the guard chain. (raised by 1/6 agents)
9. In `src/sqllens/safety/rule_sets.py`, `RefusalRedactingRunner` skips its WARNING log whenever a refusal's `__cause__` is not a guard error, assuming the guard already logged it. Raw guard functions in `safety/readonly.py` and `safety/rls.py` raise from sqlglot errors without logging, and only the runner wrappers make those refusals log today. No test pins this. (raised by 1/6 agents)
